1.0 Institutional Framework
1.1 This Regulation, issued pursuant to the Pension Reform Act, 2014 (as
amended), applies to the investment, custody, and management of all pension
fund assets under the Contributory Pension Scheme (CPS), including:
a) Retirement Savings Accounts (RSAs) administered by Pension Fund
Administrators (PFAs);
b) Pension funds managed under Approved Existing Schemes (AES);
c) Pension funds administered by Closed Pension Fund Administrators
(CPFAs).
1.2 In the event of any inconsistency between the provisions of this Regulation and
other investment guidelines previously issued by the Commission, the
provisions of this Regulation shall prevail to the extent of such inconsistency,
without prejudice to the overriding provisions of the Pension Reform Act, 2014
(as amended).
1.3 Pension Fund Custodians (PFCs) shall only act on written instructions, including
authenticated electronic instructions, from PFAs in respect of the investment
and management of pension fund assets held in their custody. Such instructions
shall be in accordance with the Pension Reform Act, 2014 (as amended) and
relevant Commission guidelines.
1.4 In discharging their contractual functions to PFAs, the PFCs shall not contract
out the custody of pension fund assets to third parties, except for allowable
investments made outside Nigeria. The PFC shall obtain prior approval from the
Commission before engaging a global Custodian for such allowable foreign
investments.
1.5 The PFAs shall not contract out the investment or management of pension fund
assets to third parties in the discharge of their contractual obligations to
Contributors, except as expressly permitted under the Pension Reform Act,
2014 (as amended), this Regulation, or any subsequent circulars or
guidelines issued by the Commission. In all such cases, the PFA shall retain
ultimate fiduciary responsibility and oversight for the assets.

1.6 The PFAs shall maintain a Multi-Fund Structure as provided in this Regulation,
to govern the investment of pension fund assets of RSA Funds.
1.7 In addition to the requirements of other guidelines issued by the Commission on
corporate governance, ethics and business practices, each PFA shall establish
an Investment Strategy Committee as well as a Risk Management Committee,
in compliance with Section 78 of the Pension Reform Act, 2014 (“the Act” or
“PRA 2014”).
1.8 The Investment Strategy Committee, in addition to other functions specified in
the Act, shall formulate internal investment strategies to enable compliance with
this Regulation, taking into cognizance the macro-economic environment as
well as the investment objectives and risk profile of the respective Funds. The
internal investment strategies shall be approved by the PFA in a formal Board
Meeting at least once every year or as frequently as changes occur in the
macroeconomic environment that may affect pension fund assets.
1.9 The Risk Management Committee shall determine the acceptable risk profile of
each investment portfolio, draw up risk assessment and measurement systems,
monitor their portfolio against risk tolerance limits, as well as all other functions
relating to risk management specified in the PRA 2014 and as may be
determined by the PFA’s Board and the Commission, from time to time. The
Risk Management Committee shall render a report of its activities to the PFA’s
Board and the Commission at least once every quarter.
1.10 Each of the Committees in Sections 1.6 and 1.7 above shall have at least one
Non-Executive Director with relevant skills and experience as a member. In
addition, an Independent Director shall chair the Risk Management Committee.
1.11 The Commission shall provide the necessary guidelines on the investment of
Pension Fund Assets outside the territory of the Federal Republic of Nigeria as
and when the need arises.

2.0 Definition of Terms
2.1 AAIOFI: The Accounting and Auditing Organization for Islamic Financial
Institutions (AAOIFI) is an Islamic international autonomous not-for-profit
corporate body that prepares accounting, auditing, governance, ethics and
Shari’ah standards for Islamic financial institutions and the industry.
2.2 Alternative Investments: Asset classes and investment vehicles that fall
outside the scope of traditional investments, such as Private Equity,
Infrastructure Fund, REITS, etc.
2.3 Asset-Backed Securities (ABS): Certificates, whether written or electronic,
issued by a Special Purpose Vehicle (SPV), the repayment of which shall be
derived from the cash flow of the pool of assets, in accordance with the terms
and conditions of the transaction. Assets used in the term Asset-backed
securities refer to loans receivable or other similar financial assets with an
expected cash payment stream, e.g. receivables, mortgage loans, leases, etc.
2.4 Bank: A commercial or merchant bank licensed by the Central Bank of Nigeria
(CBN).
2.5 Central Securities Depository: Is an institution integrated with an Exchange
to clear and settle transactions traded on an Exchange and act as a depository
for certificates of investments.
2.6 Commission: National Pension Commission, established under the Pension
Reform Act (PRA) 2014.
2.7 Commodities: Any produce, item, commodity, article, index, right, or interest of
any nature as defined in the Investment and Securities Act (ISA) 2025, subject
to guidelines issued by the Commission from time to time.
2.8 Conventional or Non-Shari’ah Compliant instruments: Refers to Financial
securities that do not comply with Shari’ah principles and are not sanctioned by
Revised Regulation on Investment of Pension Fund Assets

the Financial Regulatory Advisory Council of Experts.
2.9 CPFA: Closed Pension Fund Administrator licensed by the Commission.
2.10 Depositary Notes (DN): Debt instrument issued by a depositary bank. The
notes representing ownership of bonds denominated in a local currency held in
custody in the same jurisdiction where the underlying bonds are traded.
2.11 Depositary Receipts (DR): Negotiable financial instrument issued by a
depositary bank. It represents shares in a foreign company and trades on the
local stock exchanges in the investor’s country.
2.12 Eligible Instruments: Categories of financial assets and investment vehicles
approved by the Commission into which Pension Fund Administrators (PFAs)
may invest pension fund assets, in accordance with the provisions of the
Pension Reform Act 2014 and the Regulation on Investment of Pension
Fund Assets.
2.13 Eligible States and Local Governments or Eligible Listed or Unlisted
Corporate Entities: entities that are fully implementing the Contributory
Pension Scheme (CPS), as confirmed by the Commission on its website.
2.14 Exchange Traded Fund (ETF): A unit trust scheme or an open-ended
investment company that issues unleveraged securities or units listed on a
securities exchange recognized or registered by the Securities & Exchange
Commission (SEC) in Nigeria and tracks the performance of specified securities
or assets, which includes but is not limited to equities, basket of assets, indices,
commodity prices, foreign currency rates or any other appropriate benchmark
approved by SEC from time to time subject to guidelines issued by the
Commission.
2.15 Financial Regulatory Advisory Council of Experts (FRACE): Is an advisory
body on Islamic Banking and Finance established by the Central Bank of Nigeria
(CBN) to advise on matters relating to the Islamic commercial jurisprudence for
the effective regulation and supervision of Non-Interest Financial Institutions

and products in Nigeria.
2.16 Forward Rate Agreement (FRA): A derivative contract between two parties to
lock in an agreed interest rate to be applied on a principal amount for a specified
future period.
2.17 Gharar: Any commercial transaction associated with uncertainty, deception and
excessive speculation “the sale of what is not yet present”, such as crops not
yet harvested or fish not yet netted.
2.18 Licensed Pension Fund Operators (LPFOs): Entities that have been duly
authorized by the Commission to carry out specific functions within Nigeria’s
pension industry, in line with the provisions of the PRA 2014.
2.19 Margin Account: An account maintained with a lender, either a bank or broker,
which records the buying and selling of securities by the bank or broker, for
themselves or their clients, through loans or credits.
2.20 Market Participants: Market participants are individuals or entities that actively
engage in a market, whether it's buying, selling, or facilitating transactions. They
can be individuals, businesses, or institutions involved in various activities, such
as trading, investing, or providing goods and services within a specific market.
2.21 Mortgage-Backed Securities (MBS): MBS are Securities whose repayments
shall be derived from the cash flows of real estate or real estate-related assets
in accordance with the terms and conditions of the transaction.
2.22 Mudarabah: Is a form of Islamic equity-based partnership contract, commonly
known as a profit-sharing contract. It is a profit-sharing and loss-bearing
partnership contract where the capital provider contributes the capital while the
manager provides managerial skills to manage the mudarabah accordingly.
2.23 Multilateral Development Finance Organizations (MDFOs): Organizations

formed between three or more nations to work on development issues related
to all the countries in the respective organizations e.g. World Bank Group,
African Finance Corporation, and African Development Bank. The Federal
Ministry of Finance shall approve such eligible MDFOs.
2.24 Non-Interest compliant instruments: Financial securities and specialist
investment funds that comply with the provisions of Islamic Commercial
Jurisprudence (Shari’ah) and any other established non- interest principles, as
approved by the Advisory Council of Experts or any other body constituted by
the SEC and/or CBN or jointly by the two institutions.
2.25 Options: A Contractual agreement that gives the holder the right, but not the
obligation, to buy or sell an underlying asset at a predetermined price on or
before a specified date.
2.26 Pension Fund Assets: Pension assets under management and custody of
Licensed Pension Operators.
2.27 PFA: Pension Fund Administrator licensed by the Commission to manage
pension funds and assets.
2.28 PFC: A Pension Fund Custodian licensed by the Commission for the sole
purpose of keeping custody of pension funds and assets in trust for employees,
as well as beneficiaries of the RSA and other retirement benefit schemes.
2.29 PRA 2014: The Pension Reform Act 2014 is the Act that repeals the Pension
Reform Act no.2, 2004 and enacts the Pension Reform Act 2014 to continue to
govern and regulate the administration of the uniform contributory pension
scheme for both the public and private sectors in Nigeria.
2.30 Primary Market: A market by which companies can raise fresh capital by
issuing securities (e.g. shares and debentures, etc.) to the investing public.
2.31 Private and Public Companies: In line with Sections 22 and 24 of the
Revised Regulation on Investment of Pension Fund Assets
Page 9 of 92

Company and Allied Matters Act 2020, and without prejudice to other provisions
of the definitions, a private company shall be so designated in its Memorandum
of Association and shall have a total number of members not exceeding 50
persons. Any company other than a private company shall be a public company
and its memorandum shall state that it is a public company.
2.32 Private Equity Fund: Any designated pool of investment capital targeted at all
stages of private equity investment from start-ups to large buy-outs, including
those held by corporate entities, limited partnerships and other investment
vehicles, including Fund of Funds.
2.33 Ratings: The evaluation of the credit risk of an instrument in case of debt, a
bank for deposit placements and a company with respect to guarantees. A credit
rating of “A-” or “A+” is considered to be an “A” rating under this Regulation.
Similarly, a credit rating of “BBB- “or “BBB+” is considered to be a “BBB” rating.
Please refer to the mapping in Appendix 1.
2.34 Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs): Company or Trust Scheme that owns,
operates, or finances income-generating real estate and allows investors to pool
funds to invest in property-related assets without directly owning or managing
the properties.
2.35 Related Persons or Related Parties: Natural persons related by blood,
adoption or marriage; legal entities, one of which has control or significant
influence over the other, or both of which are controlled by some other person
or entity; a corporate entity where any of the aforementioned holds 5% or more
beneficial interest; and any other relationship that can be reasonably construed
as related persons or parties.
2.36 REPO: Repurchase/ Reverse Repurchase Agreement (REPO) is a contractual
arrangement between two parties, where one party agrees to sell securities to
another party at a specified price with a commitment to buy the securities back
at a later date.

2.37 Safekeeping Receipts: A document issued by a financial institution (like a bank
or brokerage firm) acknowledging that it is holding an asset on behalf of another
party. It serves as a confirmation that the asset is being stored securely and that
the institution is responsible for its safekeeping.
2.38 Secondary Market: A market, where securities initially issued in the primary
market are bought and sold.
2.39 Securities include:
a) Debentures, stocks, bonds or Sukuk issued or proposed to be issued by a
government;
b) Debentures, shares, bonds, Sukuk, or notes issued or proposed to be issued
by a body corporate;
c) Any right or option in respect of any such debentures, stocks, Shares, bonds,
Sukuk, or notes; and
d) Commodities futures, contracts, options and other derivatives, and the term
securities include those securities in the category of the securities listed in
(a) - (c) above which may be transferred by means of any electronic mode
approved by SEC and which may be deposited, kept or stored with any
licensed depository or custodian company as provided under the ISA 2025.
2.40 Securities Exchange: Means an exchange or an approved trading facility
(Composite or Non-composite) as defined in the ISA 2025.
2.41 State/Local Governments: Means all the State and Local Governments of the
Federal Republic of Nigeria, including the Federal Capital Territory
Administration (FCTA) and Area Councils in the FCT, which are listed in the
Constitution of the Federal Republic of Nigeria, 1999 (as amended).
2.42 Sukuk: Refers to investment certificates or notes of equal value which
evidences undivided interest/ownership of tangible assets, usufructs and

services or 351 SEC Rules; June 2013 investment in the assets of particular
projects or special investment activity using Shari’ah principles and concepts
approved by the SEC.
2.43 Supra-national Bonds or Supranational Sukuk: Means Debt instruments
issued by Multilateral Development Finance Organizations, of which Nigeria is
a member and its membership approved by the Federal Ministry of Finance.
2.44 Swaps: Financial derivative contract in which two parties agree to exchange
(or "swap") sets of cash flows or financial obligations over a specified period,
based on predetermined terms.
2.45 Wakala Bil-Istithmar: Is an Islamic agency contract whereby Islamic financial
institutions manage funds on behalf of their customers. This involves providing
agency (wakala) charges against specific fund management fees.
2.46 Private and Public Companies: In line with Sections 22 and 24 of the
Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020, and without prejudice to other
provisions of the definitions, a private company shall be so designated in its
Memorandum of Association and shall have a total number of members not
exceeding 50 persons. Any company other than a private company shall be a
public company, and its memorandum shall state that it is a public company.

3.0 General Principles
3.1 PFAs shall invest pension fund assets with the objectives of safety and the
maintenance of fair returns.
3.2 An instrument or institution seeking pension fund investment shall be rated by
at least two rating agencies, one of which shall be a rating agency incorporated
in Nigeria and registered with the SEC.
3.3 In the event of rating agencies giving different rating grades on a particular
instrument, issue, or issuer, the lower rating grade obtainable in the market shall
apply to determine the relevant maximum investment limit.
3.4 By virtue of Section 10 (2) of the PRA 2014, all interests, dividends, profits, and
other incomes accruable to pension funds and assets shall not be taxable.
3.5 PFAs shall recruit and retain personnel with relevant skills in the Investment
Department.
3.6 PFAs shall not invest Pension Fund Assets in instruments that are subject to
any type of prohibition or limitation on the sale or purchase of such instrument,
except for open/close-end/hybrid funds and specialist investment funds allowed
by this Regulation.
3.7 PFAs shall not trade on margin accounts with pension fund assets.
3.8 PFAs shall not engage in borrowing or lending of pension fund assets except
under the Securities Lending Arrangement or Repurchase Agreements
(REPOs) guidelines issued by the Commission.
3.9 PFAs shall not trade in financial instruments with pension fund assets at prices
that are prejudicial to the pension fund assets.
Revised Regulation on Investment of Pension Fund Assets

3.10 Pension fund assets shall only be invested in bonds, Sukuk, or other debt
instruments issued by eligible MDFOs, State/Local Governments, and
Corporate Entities that are fully implementing the Contributory Pension
Scheme. The Commission shall publish on its website, from time to time, the
lists of compliant State/Local Governments and Corporate Entities.
3.11 Pension fund assets shall only be invested in bonds, Sukuk or other debt
instruments of MDFOs and SPV that are implementing a pension arrangement
approved by the Commission.
3.12 Notwithstanding the provision of 3.10 and 3.11 above, evidence of pension
contribution remittance under the Contributory Pension Scheme may not be
required where:
i. The MDFO has an existing pension arrangement for its personnel.
ii. The SPV is a non-operating or Project SPV whose sponsor complies with
the requirements of the Contributory Pension Scheme.
3.13 PFAs are to ensure that appropriate legal and financial due diligence are
undertaken on all Prospectus/Offer Documents of all allowable instruments prior
to investment.
3.14 Pursuant to 3.13 above, PFAs shall take into consideration the following
amongst others, in corporate entities or specialist investment funds in which
pension fund assets are to be invested:
i. Rules governing the Board of the corporate entity or Fund;
ii. Continuous disclosure rules of material events in the corporate entity or
Fund; and
iii. Adequate disclosures of the financial condition of the corporate entity or
Fund, in the annual financial statements, which shall be audited by an
independent firm of chartered accountants registered with the Financial
Reporting Council (FRC).

3.15 PFAs/CPFAs shall incorporate Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG)
factors into their investment decision-making processes, emphasizing
governance and responsible investing, encouraging collaboration and inclusive
growth, and allocating long-term assets to priority sectors that promote
sustainable national development or other thematic areas as designated by the
Commission.
4.0 Authorized Markets
4.1 Primary and Secondary market transactions shall be carried out on exchanges
approved in line with the provisions of the ISA 2025.
4.2 All primary market investments by PFAs in ordinary or preference shares of
eligible corporate entities shall only be through public offerings, listing by
introduction or private placement approved by the SEC.
4.3 All secondary market trading of pension assets, shall occur on securities
exchanges or trading platforms recognized by the SEC.
4.4 All primary market investments by PFAs in bonds, Sukuk, debenture and other
debt instruments issued by eligible corporate entities shall be through public
offering or private placement arrangements approved by SEC. PFAs may invest
in bonds or Sukuk issued by publicly listed companies through private
placement arrangements provided they fulfill the requirements in Section 6.2.4
of this Regulation.
4.5 All primary market investments by PFAs in participation units of Open, Close-
End, Hybrid Investment Funds, including ETFs, Specialist Investment Funds
(REITs, Infrastructure Fund and Private Equity Fund) and other Non-interest
compliant instruments shall be through public offering or private placement
arrangements, except when:
i. Trading with participation units of Open/Closed-end or Hybrid Investment
Funds on the memorandum list of a securities exchange registered by the
SEC or Specialist Investment Funds (Infrastructure and Private Equity) and

Non-Interest (Shari’ah) Compliant Investment Funds registered by SEC.
ii. Acquiring or trading in securities of an eligible Nigerian corporate entity,
listed or quoted in an Offshore Securities Exchange.
5.0 Allowable Instruments
Pension fund assets shall be invested in the following allowable instruments:
5.1 Bonds, Sukuk, Treasury Bills, Depository Receipts, Promissory Notes and other
securities issued by the Federal Government of Nigeria and CBN or their
agencies as well as Special Purpose Vehicles and Companies created/owned
by the Federal Government of Nigeria, provided that the Federal Government
of Nigeria or the CBN guarantees the securities.
5.2 Bonds and Sukuk issued by eligible State and Local Governments or State
Government Agencies or wholly owned companies of the State Government, or
any other arrangement of which a State or Local Government is the ultimate
beneficiary, provided that such securities are fully guaranteed by Irrevocable
Standing Payment Orders (ISPOs) against State's Federal Allocation or external
guarantees by MDFOs with a minimum credit rating of ‘AA’.
5.3 Sukuk, debentures, redeemable/ convertible preference shares, and other debt
instruments issued by public and private corporate entities, Asset-Backed
Securities including Mortgage Bonds, Mortgage-Backed Securities, and
Infrastructure Bonds / Sukuk.
5.4 Debt securities issued by corporate entities and guaranteed by the
Federal/State Governments, MDFOs, or any agency backed by a sovereign or
Development Finance Institution with a minimum credit rating of AA.
5.5 Eligible agricultural sector instruments, such as debt securities, equities, and
infrastructure projects within the agricultural value chain, provided such
instruments meet the eligibility, quality, valuation, and risk management
requirements specified under the Pension Reform Act, 2014 (as amended), and
this Regulation.

i. Government Sukuk (including Islamic Treasury Bills and Euro Sukuk)
issued by FGN, CBN or FGN Agencies and Infrastructure Sukuk, backed

ii. Corporate Sukuk (including Shari’ah-compliant ABS, MBS, DNs, Euro

5.7 Ordinary Shares of Public Limited Liability Companies whether listed, unlisted

5.8 Money Market Instruments of Banks and Commercial Papers issued by eligible

5.9 Open/ Close-ended/ Hybrid Investment Funds, including Exchange Traded

5.10 Specialist Investment Funds whose underlying assets are tangible physical

i. Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) registered by SEC.

iii. Infrastructure Funds registered with SEC.
iv. Exchange Traded Derivatives.

5.11 Supranational Bonds and Supranational Sukuk issued by eligible MDFOs
approved by the Federal Ministry of Finance.
5.12 DRs/Ns and Eurobonds issued by eligible Nigerian corporate entities as well as

securities exchange that is a member of the World Federation of Exchanges
(WFE).
5.13 SKRs tradable on an Exchange recognized by the SEC.
6.0 Quality Requirements for Allowable Instruments
6.1 Rating Requirements
The following rating requirements shall apply:
6.1.1 All ratings shall be undertaken by rating agencies incorporated in Nigeria and
registered with the SEC or foreign rating agencies recognized by the SEC.
6.1.2 Bonds and Sukuks issued by States, Local Governments, and Corporate
Entities as well as Infrastructure Bonds and other allowable debt instruments in
which pension fund assets are to be invested, shall have a minimum credit rating
of ‘A’ issued by, at least, two rating agencies, one of which shall be a rating
agency incorporated in Nigeria and registered with SEC.
6.1.3 Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 6.1.2, PFAs may invest a maximum
of 20% of pension assets under management in any combination of debt
instruments issued by States, Local Governments, and Corporate Entities, with
a credit rating of ‘BBB’ issued by, at least, two rating agencies, one of which
shall be a rating agency incorporated in Nigeria and registered with SEC.
6.1.4 The money market instruments of any bank shall have a minimum credit rating
of ‘BBB’ issued by at least two rating agencies, one of which shall be a rating
agency incorporated in Nigeria and registered with SEC to qualify for investment
of pension funds.

6.1.5 For Commercial Papers (CPs), pension fund assets shall only be invested in
CPs of Corporate Entities with a minimum credit rating of ‘A’ issued by at least
two rating agencies, one of which shall be a rating agency incorporated in
Nigeria. However, the CPs of ‘BBB’ rated corporate entities can be considered
for investment, if guaranteed by any agency backed by a sovereign or
Development Finance Institution with a minimum credit rating of AA.
6.1.6 Any Eurobond issued by an eligible Nigerian Corporate Entity in which pension
fund assets are to be invested shall have a credit rating not lower than the
sovereign rating of Nigeria at the time of issuance by a SEC recognized rating
agency.
6.1.7 Bond, Sukuk, and other allowable debt instruments issued by eligible MDFOs
in which pension fund assets are to be invested shall have a minimum credit
rating of ‘BBB’ issued by a SEC recognized rating agency.
6.1.8 The minimum rating specified above shall be maintained throughout the tenor
of the investments.
6.1.9 At the expiration of the specified ratings above, the pension fund may retain
such investment for a maximum of 6 months after the expiration.
6.1.10 If at any time an existing investment is no longer authorized as a result of a
credit rating downgrade, resulting in a new rating that is not more than one grade
below the stipulated minimum, the pension fund may retain such investment to
maturity.
6.1.11 If at any time an existing investment is no longer authorized, as a result of either
a credit rating withdrawal or a credit rating downgrade by more than one grade
or for any other reason, the PFA shall forward its exit strategy to the Commission
within 10 working days.

6.1.12 PFAs shall not rely only on ratings assigned by Rating Companies, as they are
only complementary to PFAs’ internal due diligence and analysis before
investing in any instrument or issuer.
6.2 Other Quality Requirements
6.2.1 Requirements for Bonds Issued by MDFOs
Pension Fund Assets can only be invested in Bonds or Sukuks issued by
MDFOs if:
i. The bonds/debt instruments meet the rating requirements in Section 6.1.
ii. The MDFO is recognized by FMOF.
iii. A minimum of 20% of the proceeds is utilized for projects within Nigeria.
iv. The amount on issue shall not be less than N20 billion.
6.2.2 Requirements for DRs/Ns
6.2.2.1 Pension Fund Assets may be invested in Depositary Receipts/Notes (DRs/Ns),
Eurobonds and Naira-denominated Depository Receipts/Notes. However, the
following minimum qualifying requirements shall apply:
i. DN and Eurobond instruments issued and guaranteed by the Federal
Government of Nigeria shall be eligible for pension fund investments.
ii. Issuers of eligible DRs, DNs and Eurobonds, which are eligible Nigerian
corporate entities, shall be registered and operating in Nigeria, as
evidenced by current relevant tax filings and other regulatory filings with the
Corporate Affairs Commission and any requisite supervisory regulatory

iii. In situations where off-shore subsidiaries are the issuing entities of the DNs

8.0 The Multi-Fund Structure
8.1 General Provisions
8.1.1 With respect to the multi-fund structure, the following shall apply:
i. The Multi-Fund Structure shall comprise seven funds, and all PFAs shall
continue to offer the Multi-Fund Structure for the RSA Fund.
ii. The seven funds shall include Fund I, Fund II, Fund III, Fund IV (Retiree
Fund), Fund V - Conservative (Micro Pension Fund), Fund V – Growth (Micro
Pension Fund), Fund VI (Non-interest Fund), which shall be split into Fund
VI Active and Fund VI Retiree Funds and Fund VII (Dollar Denominated
Fund).
iii. The funds shall differ in their exposure to variable income instruments.
iv. The exposure to variable income instruments is defined as the sum of a
PFA’s investments in Ordinary Shares and participation units of Open
Closed-ended, and Hybrid Funds; Real Estate Investment Trust;
Infrastructure Funds; and Private Equity Funds comprising its current
holdings and any future financial commitments to the acquisition of
participation units in these Funds.
v. In line with (iv) above, the maximum exposure to variable income
instruments by the Fund Types are as follows:

8.2.1 Effective from the date of implementation of the Multi-Fund Structure, the PFAs
shall allocate contributors to various Fund Types according to the following
criteria:
i. Membership of Fund I shall strictly be by formal request by a Contributor who
is 49 years and below as at his/her last birthday.
ii. Active Contributors who are 49 years and below as at their last birthdays shall
be assigned to Fund II.
iii. Active Contributors who are 50 years and above as at their last birthdays
shall be assigned to Fund III.
iv. Fund IV and VI shall strictly be for RSA retirees only.
v. Fund V shall strictly be for contributors under the Micro-pension Scheme.
vi. Fund VI shall be for contributors and retirees' who choose to have their

8.5 Fund Types
8.5.1 RSA Funds (I-IV)
8.5.1.1. The Multi-Fund Structure shall comprise Fund I, Fund II, Fund III, and Fund IV
(Retiree Fund). Funds I, II, III and IV shall differ among themselves according
to their overall exposure to variable income instruments.
8.5.2 Fund V (Micro Pension Fund)
8.5.2.1 Fund V shall be designated for contributors under the Micro Pension Scheme
and divided into two categories: a Conservative Fund (Fund V – Conservative)
and a Growth Fund (Fund V – Growth).
8.5.2.2 The Investment of the Fund shall be undertaken in accordance with the
provisions of this Regulation. The contributions shall, by default, be allocated as
follows: 60% retained for pensions and 40% available for contingent
withdrawals, or such other allocation ratio as may be determined by the
Commission from time to time through circulars or guidelines.
8.5.3 Fund VI (Non-interest Fund)
8.5.3.1 Fund VI shall be for contributors who choose to have their pension contributions
invested in Non-Interest Money and Capital Market Products.
8.5.3.2 Fund VI shall be separated into two funds for Active RSA holders and Retirees
as follows:
i. Active Non-Interest Fund (Active Fund VI): For contributors in Funds I, II and
III who have elected to move their contributions to Fund VI.
ii. Retiree Non-Interest Fund (Retiree Fund VI): For Retirees in Fund IV who
move their contributions to Retiree Fund VI.
8.5.3.3 Ethical Principles: The following ethical principles shall apply:
i. Fund VI assets shall not be invested in the production or trading of alcohol,
pornography, weaponry, gambling/betting, speculation, interest earning

and as may be determined by FRACE from time to time.
ii. Fund VI shall be based on the principles of Wakala Bil-Istithmar (investment
agency contract) with the PFA acting as the investment agent for active RSA
contributors in Fund VI.
iii. The principle of Mudarabah contract (profit-sharing and loss-bearing
partnership) shall be used for retirees in Fund IV who opted for Fund VI.
iv. Fund VI assets are to be invested in instruments that are free from
speculation and uncertainty that might lead to destruction or loss, otherwise
known as ‘Gharar’ under Islamic commercial jurisprudence.
v. Pursuant to (i) above, the fundamental value of a security with respect to the
annual income it may bring such as dividends, is to be considered by PFAs
before future price considerations. Derivative products such as Futures
Contracts, Swaps, Options and Forwards are considered as speculative and
uncertain.
vi. PFAs shall obtain sufficient knowledge (number of units, terms of the
sale/contract, and monetary worth) of the instrument(s) intended to be
exchanged before taking investment decisions on Fund VI assets.
8.5.3.4 Eligibility Requirements
i. RSA holders in Fund I, Fund II and Fund III are eligible to move their RSA
contributions to Fund VI (Active Fund VI).
ii. Retirees in Fund IV are eligible to move their RSA contributions to Fund VI
(Retiree Fund VI).
iii. RSA contributors in Fund III can move their contributions directly to Retiree
Fund VI at the time of retirement.
iv. The Commission shall determine the participation of Micro Pension
Contributors in due course.

10.0 Violations of Investment Limits
10.1 Limits imposed by this Regulation may be temporarily violated in cases of assets
revaluation. However, where such violation results from market appreciation in the
value of securities, the PFA shall immediately notify the Commission and make no
further purchases of such security until the portfolio is rebalanced.
10.2 If at any time a PFA willfully violates any of the investment limits so prescribed in
Section 9.0 of this Regulation, the PFA may maintain the investments but shall not
make any additional investments in that instrument until there is rebalancing. The
rebalancing shall be done within thirty (30) days from the day of violation. Where there
is a loss as a result of the violation, the PFA shall refund the loss to the Fund. In
addition, the PFA shall pay a penalty for violation of the approved limit, as may be
determined by the Commission.
10.3 If a bank fails to fulfill the rating requirements stated in this Regulation, the PFA shall
divest itself of all money market instruments issued by the bank within the following 3
months, while Commercial papers issued by both banks and other corporate entities
may be held till maturity.

13.0 Closed Pension Funds and Approved Existing Schemes
13.1 Pursuant to Section 50 (1) (f) of the PRA 2014, all investments made prior to the
commencement of the Act in assets which are contrary to Section 86 of the Act, may
be maintained by entities whose existing schemes have been approved by the
Commission to continue to exist. This is, however, subject to appropriate Guidelines
that may be issued by the Commission.
13.2 CPFAs and Approved Existing Schemes (AESs) may continue to invest in approved
asset classes and securities (including real estate properties and foreign investments)
provided that they do not exceed the investment limits specified in their Internal
Investment Guidelines as approved by the Commission.
13.3 In line with 13.2 above, the investment limits in the Internal Investment Guidelines
shall be set by the Trustees of the Fund.
13.4 Notwithstanding the provisions of Section 13.2 above, CPFAs/AESs shall not convert
Naira into foreign currencies for investments outside Nigeria, without compliance with
Section 87(2) of PRA 2014 and Guidelines for Investment in Foreign Currency
Dominated Assets to be issued by the Commission from time to time.
